1. A student investigates how the period $T$ of a simple pendulum varies with the maximum speed $v$ of the pendulum's bob by releasing the pendulum from rest from different initial angles. A graph of the variation of $T$ with $v$ is plotted.
[Graph: $T$ / s (2.09 to 2.16) against $v$ / m s$^{-1}$ (0.00 to 2.25); five data points with error bars at about v = 0.70, 1.15, 1.45, 1.75, 2.10 rising with increasing gradient]
(a) Suggest, by reference to the graph, why it is unlikely that the relationship between $T$ and $v$ is linear. [1]
(b) Determine the fractional uncertainty in $v$ when $T = 2.115$ s, correct to one significant figure. [2]
(c) The student hypothesizes that the relationship between $T$ and $v$ is $T = a + bv^2$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. To verify this hypothesis a graph showing the variation of $T$ with $v^2$ is plotted. The graph shows the data and the line of best fit.
[Graph: $T$ / s (2.09 to 2.16) against $v^2$ / m$^2$ s$^{-2}$ (0 to 5); data points with error bars and a straight line of best fit]
Determine $b$, giving an appropriate unit for $b$. [3]
(d) The lines of the minimum and maximum gradient are shown.
[Graph: same $T$ against $v^2$ data with maximum- and minimum-gradient lines drawn, intercepts near 2.095 s and 2.101 s]
Estimate the absolute uncertainty in $a$. [2]
